item.title: Asian Games | China overturns 11-point deficit to win men's 10m air pistol team gold
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- Three shooting gold medals were decided at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Thursday, with China staging a dramatic comeback from 11 points down to claim the men's 10m air pistol team gold. The men's 10m air pistol team event featured a strong field, with China, South Korea and India among the medal contenders. With a large number of entries, qualification was carried out in two groups. Indonesia emerged as a surprising contender in the first group, with Muhamad Iqbal Raia Prabowo scoring 589 points and Sulthanul Aulia Maruf 583. China's Bu Shuaihang and Xie Yu posted 583 and 578 respectively, leaving Indonesia with an 11-point lead after the first group. The duel between China's Hu Kai and Indonesia's Wira Sukmana became the focus of the second group. Hu shot a steady 292 points over the first three series, while Sukmana managed 284, cutting Indonesia's lead to three points. The contest tightened in the second half, with Hu finishing on 582 points. Sukmana recovered, but needed a 10 on his final shot to secure the title, he scored a nine and finished with 571. China and Indonesia were tied on 1,743 points, with China taking gold on the higher number of inner tens, 70 to 57. Indonesia settled for silver, while Japan took bronze with 1,730 points. After helping China complete the comeback, Hu said he had not known the exact scores at the start of the competition. "There were ups and downs during the match, and when things weren't going well, I just tried to make adjustments," Hu said. In the individual final, Uzbekistan's Vladimir Svechnikov took gold with 244.3 points, while Hu and Bu claimed silver and bronze respectively. In the skeet mixed team event, China's Jiang Yiting and Lu Jianlin both delivered strong performances to win gold with 52 hits. South Korea took silver and India bronze. It was Jiang's third gold medal of the Games, following her victories in the women's skeet team and individual events on Wednesday. "My first Asian Games were in Hangzhou, where I won one gold, one silver and one bronze. This time I made a big step forward, and I'm really satisfied to have won three gold medals," Jiang said. ■

item.title: Xi lands in U.S. for state visit, greeted by Trump at airport
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan step out of the airplane cabin upon their arrival at Joint Base Andrews in the United States on Sept. 23, 2026. Xi arrived at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday afternoon for a state visit to the United States at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump. Xi and Peng were warmly greeted by Trump and his wife, Melania Trump, at the airport in a rare planeside welcome. (Xinhua/Liu Bin) WASHINGTON, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday afternoon for a state visit to the United States at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump. Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, were warmly greeted by Trump and his wife, Melania Trump, at the airport in a rare planeside welcome. American children presented flowers to Xi and Peng. The honor guards lined up on both sides of the red carpet to pay their respects. The welcome ceremony also included a 21-gun salute, the playing of the national anthems of both countries and a military flyover. In a written speech, Xi extended sincere greetings and best wishes to the U.S. people on behalf of the Chinese people. China and the United States are both great countries, and the two peoples are both great peoples, Xi said in the speech, adding that the two peoples have maintained friendly exchanges for a long time and their interests are deeply intertwined. China and the United States should be partners, not rivals, he said, noting that the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand, and that the two countries can help each other succeed and advance the well-being of the whole world. Xi noted that he and Trump agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability during Trump's visit to China in May, which has provided strategic guidance for the future development of bilateral ties. China and the United States should work in the same direction, promote a stable relationship featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences, and promises of peace, Xi said. He said China and the United States, as two major countries, should find a right way to get along in the new era. Xi emphasized that the world is developing and times are changing, but the historical logic of peaceful coexistence between China and the United States has not changed, the goodwill of friendly exchanges between the two peoples has not changed, and the general expectations of the international community for China and the United States have not changed. Xi said he looks forward to having in-depth exchanges with Trump on major issues concerning bilateral relations and the world situation, constantly enriching the connotation of the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and expanding the space for exchanges and cooperation in various fields between the two countries. Xi said he also looks forward to engaging extensively with people from all walks of life in the United States to deepen friendship. With joint efforts, Xi said he believes the visit is sure to be fruitful, and will enhance the well-being of the two peoples and add hope for world peace. On Xi's way from the airport to his hotel by car, representatives of overseas Chinese and students gathered on both sides of the road, waving the national flags of China and the United States to warmly welcome his visit. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives at Joint Base Andrews on Sept. 23, 2026, for a state visit to the United States at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump. item.title: China's extended holiday set to boost long-haul travel, border crossings
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- China's upcoming Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays bring travelers a major bonus this year: extra time for longer journeys and extended stays. Separated by three working days, the three-day and seven-day holiday periods can be bridged into a 13-day break running from Sept. 25 to Oct. 7. REACHING FAROFF DESTINATIONS For Shanghai white-collar worker Zheng Bing, the extended break means she can leave before the Mid-Autumn Festival, which falls on Sept. 25 per the lunar calendar, and spend more time in Malaysia. "This allows me to enjoy my vacation at a leisurely pace," said Zheng, whose plans mirror a wider desire for long-haul travel over the coming holiday. Data from Chinese online travel platforms show that tours of 10 days or more are particularly popular, making up 26 percent of all bookings. Meanwhile, flight reservations for top international destinations have surged over 20 percent year on year. "Sales for international packages with stays over 10 days are up from last year," said Wang Wei, president of the Shanghai-based Spring International Travel Service (Group) Co., Ltd. Popular spots include Spain, Greece, Britain, Türkiye and Azerbaijan, the firm added. China's National Immigration Administration expects an average of about 2.25 million cross-border trips per day during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday from Sept. 25 to 27, and about 2.15 million per day during the National Day holiday from Oct. 1 to 7. Sales of tour packages to domestic long-haul destinations are also gaining momentum. On Fliggy, Alibaba Group's online travel platform, reservations to such destinations, including Urumqi in northwest China's Xinjiang, Kunming in southwest Yunnan, and Sanya in the far southern island province of Hainan, have been on the rise. Flight ticket bookings confirm this trend. According to data from Umetrip, a mobile platform for real-time flight information, the number of reservations for domestic flights flying over 2,000 km surpassed 1.74 million, a year-on-year increase of 14 percent. EXPERIENCES OUTWEIGH CHECKLIST TOURS Analysts said that more tourists are favoring special travel experiences, niche tourist destinations and customized packages, particularly when the upcoming super-long holiday makes such travel plans easier to enjoy. "For younger tourists, how to spend a vacation matters more than where to spend it," said Yang Han, a researcher with online travel platform Qunar. In the upcoming holidays, bookings for glacier hiking on Fliggy went up 50 percent from the previous year, skydiving up nearly 80 percent, and whale watching surged 200 percent. Niche tourist destinations, such as lesser-known county-level towns, are attracting tourists. Online travel platform Tongcheng predicted that tourists will stay 3.2 days longer in county-level destinations on average compared with the same period last year. Tourists are also discovering new sides of cities and towns beyond their famous landmarks or cultural heritage. On online travel platforms, hotel bookings and ticket reservations have surged in cities hosting concerts, sporting events and cultural activities. QUALITY TOUR PACKAGES IN DEMAND As more tourists opt for immersive, in-depth experiences rather than hurried sightseeing, they are also on the hunt for better accommodation and higher-quality travel services. A longer holiday creates more room for tourism consumption, said Cheng Chaogong at Tongcheng. "Quality and experience will become key factors," Cheng noted. The government is also on the move to make sure diverse cultural events and spending incentives are in place across the country. China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism launched a month-long national tourism promotion campaign on Sept. 22. While hosting more than 20,000 events spanning scenic trips, autumn outings, red tourism, study tours, night activities and local food to boost diverse premium tourism offerings, local governments are handing out some 310 million yuan (about 45.9 million U.S. dollars) in consumer vouchers and subsidies over the month as a way to spur tourism consumption. Zheng is about to leave for Malaysia tonight. She's eagerly anticipating her unhurried but fulfilling holiday. "I could still have time to take a rest and check the air of festivity in Shanghai after the trip," she said. ■

item.title: Service consumption outpaces goods as China's consumer market enters new stage: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- China's consumer market has entered a new stage in which goods and services are both important, with service retail sales expanding at nearly five times the pace of goods retail sales in the first eight months of this year, a structural shift captured by a new official indicator in the world's second-largest consumer market. Total retail sales of consumer goods and services rose 2.5 percent year on year in the January-August period this year, with service retail sales up 4.9 percent and goods retail sales up 1 percent, officials and experts said at the China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk platform hosted by Xinhua News Agency. In June this year, the National Bureau of Statistics released the "total retail sales of consumer goods and services" indicator for the first time, a move analysts say better reflects the full picture of consumption as services become an increasingly important driver of domestic demand. "As per capita income rises, it is an objective economic law that service consumption grows faster than goods consumption," said Lin Jian, vice president of the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation under the Ministry of Commerce. The shift is visible in changing consumer behavior. Zhang Weihua, deputy director of the Shandong Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism, said consumers are moving from "buying goods" to "buying peace of mind" and from "functional consumption" to "experiential consumption," seeking immersive, interactive and emotionally rewarding experiences. For his part, Chen Chunhui, chairman of Xiamen International Cruise Home Port Group Co., Ltd., said that "cruise consumption, from ship to shore, integrates dining, lodging, transport, sightseeing, shopping and entertainment, reflecting the growing demand for composite experiences." In Xiamen, a coastal city in east China's Fujian Province, the Xiamen International Cruise Home Port, one of China's four pilot demonstration cruise transport ports, saw inbound cruise ship calls rise 33 percent year on year in the first half, with passenger numbers up about 180 percent, according to Chen. "In the long run, sustainable consumption growth hinges on a virtuous cycle between consumption upgrading and industrial upgrading, with demand-side policies pushing manufacturers toward greener and smarter production," Lin said. On the policy front, China has been steering demand toward green and smart products through trade-in programs for automobiles and home appliances. The leverage ratio of subsidy funds rose from 1:7.8 in 2025 to 1:10.3 this year, according to Lin. China is the world's second-largest consumer market. The country targets relatively fast growth in total consumer goods and services consumption, with total retail sales of consumer goods reaching around 60 trillion yuan (about 8.3 trillion U.S. dollars) by 2030. It also aims to cultivate 10-trillion-yuan-level markets in green, intelligent and health-related consumption. China also aims to attract 190 million inbound tourist visits a year by 2030, with annual inbound tourism spending exceeding 150 billion U.S. dollars, according to a new five-year tourism development plan unveiled in July this year. The plan signals the country's expanding efforts to draw overseas visitors as it seeks to boost consumption. Lin said new growth areas such as "AI plus consumption" are expected to expand rapidly, providing broad space for the upgrading of goods and services consumption. "Service consumption and goods consumption will become more deeply integrated, with their boundaries increasingly blurred. But what remains unchanged is starting from user demand and continuously turning real needs into products," said Zhang Dandan, head of the Changsha New Consumption Research Institute. "During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China's service consumption is expected to accelerate further," Lin added. ■

item.title: China issues revised regulations on implementation of audit law
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating revised regulations on the implementation of the audit law. The revised regulations, which consist of 7 chapters and 64 articles, will take effect on Dec. 1. Highlighting the need to refine and improve audit supervision, the regulations specify the scope and content of audits over fiscal revenues and expenditures, and bring the management and use of state-owned resources into the scope of special audit investigations, among others. To ensure that audit work is free from interference, the regulations add provisions on a registration and reporting system for any unwarranted attempts to inquire about or interfere with audit matters. All departments of the State Council and local authorities at all levels shall strengthen overall coordination, oversee rectification of problems uncovered in audits, and establish and improve relevant systems. ■

item.title: Quotable Quotes: Xi Jinping on family and country
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
Friday marks the Mid-Autumn Festival, also known as the Moon Festival, a traditional Chinese holiday when families gather to celebrate. Under the full moon, people share mooncakes and savor the joy of reunion. The moon goddess Chang'e, the Jade Rabbit, the osmanthus tree and glowing lanterns are among the timeless symbols of the festival. In Chinese culture, love for one's family is closely tied to a sense of responsibility for the country. President Xi Jinping has often spoken about this connection. Let's revisit his words and the values they reflect. ■
